newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: African mines urged to seek Canadian links.
newsitem.headline: African mines urged to seek Canadian links.

text.p: African mining companies should form alliances with Canadian companies listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange if they wanted to attract meaningful investment flows.
RBC Dominion Securities vice presidents David Scott and John Barker told an Investing in Africa mining conference on Thursday many investors faced difficulities in evaluating African investments.
Barker said that Toronto had overtaken other world stock exchanges as the major centre for international mining finance and could be a major source of funding for Africa.
He said that while many investors were concerned about the geological prospects of any mine, value for money remained the biggest buying force.
Determining this was difficult. For example, South African mining companies did not follow the North American accounting convention of amortising capital expenditure.
Instead, capital expenditure was fully depreciated in the year it was earned, giving a completely different picture to investors.
South African mines also overstated their cash cost figures by including items such as royalties instead of stating them as working or exceptional items.
"Fortuanately a number of South African companies are addressing this issue and are standardising cash costs," Barker said.
"Anglo American has indicated that their cash costs could fall by as much as $20 an ounce by changing the definitions."

To help investors, RBC Dominion Securities had modelled discounted cash flows (DCFs) for a wide range of companies to indicate absolute value and indicate the gold price premium that would be needed to achieve that.

"While the African sector is close to parity, Australia and North America would require a gold price approximately 60 percent higher than the current levels to justify the current DCF rating," Barker said.

Australian and North American premiums continued to increase, driven by continued expectations that resources would grow and the fact that there was a continual flow of funds requiring a home to go to.
This did not mean there were no good investment opportunities in Africa. But because of their ratings, they were being overlooked.
Barker said the good investments included Beatrix Mines Ltd, Harmony Gold Mining Ltd, Ashanti Goldfields Company Ltd, Evander Gold Mines Ltd and Western Areas Gold Mining Company Ltd.
"I believe that selected African mines such as Beatrix and Ashanti have the right cost and exploration profiles to merit international interest, but...the shares will not benefit," he said.

He suggested that African companies started using the same accounting conventions as North America to level the playing field. They should also transform and simplify management and head office roles and where possible transfer assets offshore."
